text:
Rasmus Dahlin missed three games in mid-October and has started quietly, but the steady parts are all there: 24:32 a night, 38 shots, ten points, and a one-timer from the right point against Columbus on November 6 that Bleacher Report's Joe Yerdon called "an absolute rocket".

Nothing in his numbers says luck. He has three goals on 2.41 expected and the Sabres' on-ice finishing is only slightly above their chances. Buffalo gets 53.7 percent of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, more than five points better than without him. His scoring rate (1.88 points per 60) actually sits below our range for him, so if anything the points should pick up.

The first overall pick of 2018 has become exactly the defenseman the Sabres hoped for. Evolving-Hockey had him 12th among 215 defensemen last season at 2.7 wins above replacement, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking rated his passing (8.2 primary shot assists per 60) in the 99th percentile among defensemen. With Buffalo just back from a 3-0 trip through California, he is the reason its process looks real.
headline: Dahlin is still the Sabres' tone setter
